items.q: Another musician that had gone to Wilberforce College and was now in Paris was a trumpet player named Jimmy Bell. Jimmy was married to an American white girl whose name was Grace Edwards and who was a singer.

ctx.x: Between Boudon's and Lizieux's, that corner was a little Harlem in the early morning when all the night spots were closed and the American musicians and entertainers gathered in those bars and the "tabac".

Another musician that had gone to Wilberforce College and was now in Paris was a trumpet player named Jimmy Bell. Jimmy was married to an American white girl whose name was Grace Edwards and who was a singer.

Other American entertainers in Paris at this time were Opal Cooper who sang at the melody bar just in front of the tabac and Boudons; Snow Fisher, a dancer and drummer; Alberta Hunter, a blues singer; Glover Compton, a singer that accompanied himself on piano; Al Brown the ex-boxing champ; Irene Bullard who had a gymnasium on rue Mansart; Marino and Norris, singers; and Edgar A. Wiggins a journalist for the Chicago Defender, a negro weekly paper. Also Cle Sadler, an alto-sax player; Ray Stokes, pianist; Harry…
